name: Mouse on Mars
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Jan St. Werner and Andi Toma, friends from the Rhineland and by Wikipedia's account born the same day in the same hospital, have spent three decades making electronic records with live drummers, Mark E. Smith and a speech program they taught to sing.

eras.title: Wibbly, barely digital
eras.text: Jan St. Werner from Cologne and Andi Toma from Düsseldorf made wordless records out of krautrock, dub, techno and ambient for London's Too Pure. By the late '90s they ran their own label, Sonig, and were in the studio with Stereolab.

years.h: Jan St. Werner and Andi Toma, friends since childhood, start a duo
years.p: Jan St. Werner of Cologne and Andi Toma of Düsseldorf form Mouse on Mars. Wikipedia says they were born on the same day in the same hospital.

years.h: Vulvaland arrives on Too Pure with no vocals
years.p: AllMusic's Sean Cooper heard "a wibbly, barely digital match of ambient texturology with experimental strains of techno, dub, and Krautrock."
years.xp:
The single Frosch came out on Too Pure the same year, and the duo landed a track on the Trance Europe Express 3 compilation.

Early Mouse on Mars had no singer: the records were all texture and rhythm.

years.h: Iaora Tahiti loosens up
years.p: Mouse on Mars' second Too Pure album is lighter and wider-ranging than the debut. A single the same year carries the title Saturday Night Worldcup Fieber.

years.h: Autoditacker is the last album for Too Pure
years.p: It is Mouse on Mars' third. The same year, Instrumentals appears on Sonig, the duo's own label.

years.h: Stereolab bring Mouse on Mars in for Dots and Loops
years.p: Mouse on Mars record and tour with [[Stereolab|f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6]], appearing on Dots and Loops and the Miss Modular EP. Jan St. Werner and [[Lætitia Sadier|9710d91f-bfbd-4f84-9c54-cb04f2a464b1]] have since sung karaoke duets together.

years.h: Glam comes out on the duo's own label
years.p: Sonig releases it, in the gap between the Too Pure years and the Thrill Jockey ones.

eras.title: A drummer sings, Mark E. Smith calls
eras.text: Thrill Jockey picked Mouse on Mars up in America just as the duo brought live instruments into the machines. Their touring drummer became a singer, the records turned toward pop, and a single led to a band with The Fall's Mark E. Smith.

yt: Full set, Double Door, Chicago, April 28, 2000
years.h: Niun Niggung puts real playing up front
years.p: Domino and Sonig release it in Europe, Thrill Jockey in the US. It is Mouse on Mars' fifth album and the first to lead with live instruments.

yt: Distroia live at Bizarre Festival, Weeze, Aug 17, 2001
years.h: Idiology keeps pushing live instruments into the electronics
years.p: Thrill Jockey also issues the singles Actionist Respoke and, in 2002, Agit Itter It.

years.cap: Jan St. Werner and Andi Toma
years.h: A drummer takes the mic on Radical Connector
years.p: Touring drummer Dodo NKishi, the third member of the live band, sings on what is Mouse on Mars' most accessible record.

years.h: Mark E. Smith shows up on Wipe That Sound
years.p: [[Mark E. Smith|35e5ce55-486d-40a4-9ab5-08de9be70d33]] of [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]] works with Jan St. Werner and Andi Toma on the single, their first collaboration.

years.h: Live 04, recorded as a three-piece
years.p: Jan St. Werner, Andi Toma and Dodo NKishi on drums, on Mouse on Mars' first live album.

years.cap: Mouse on Mars live at Open Source Festival, Düsseldorf, August 19, 2006
years.h: Mike Patton's label puts out Varcharz
years.p: Mouse on Mars release it through Sonig and [[Mike Patton|6e891631-d99c-4768-8bc2-5e5feb42881c]]'s Ipecac Recordings.

years.h: Mark E. Smith claims he's been sacked from Von Südenfed
years.p: Smith's words, as Wikipedia's Von Südenfed page archives them. Tromatic Reflexxions was out on Domino, and two December 2007 shows had been cancelled for illness.
years.xp:
Critics compared Von Südenfed to [[LCD Soundsystem|2aaf7396-6ab8-40f3-9776-a41c42c8e26b]]. Smith's answer was that LCD Soundsystem were heavily influenced by the Fall. The singles were Fledermaus Can't Get It and The Rhinohead.

The sacking talk didn't stick: Smith played with the group live again and a second album was discussed. Not enough was recorded before he died in January 2018.

eras.title: Six years off, then Berlin
eras.text: After six years without a Mouse on Mars album, the duo landed on Modeselektor's Berlin label Monkeytown, worked with a singer, a producer and a punk band, and started building their own music software.

years.cap: Mouse on Mars DJ set at Salon des Amateurs, Düsseldorf
years.h: After six years, Parastrophics
years.p: Mouse on Mars' first album since 2006 is also their first on Monkeytown, the label run by Berlin duo [[Modeselektor|8a7a4e72-a099-425f-8238-80706fc1c746]].

years.h: Dao Anh Khanh, Eric D. Clark and Las Kellies join the WOW EP
years.p: The Monkeytown EP is the duo's first recorded work with singer Dao Anh Khanh, producer Eric D. Clark and the punk band Las Kellies.

years.cap: Mouse on Mars live in concert
years.h: Berlin Music Video Awards give them Best Special Effects
years.p: Mouse on Mars take the prize at the 2013 ceremony.

years.cap: Jan St. Werner performing solo at the Goethe-Institut Boston, March 8, 2017
years.h: Synaptics closes out the Monkeytown years
years.p: It is the last Mouse on Mars release on Monkeytown before the move back to Thrill Jockey.

eras.title: Twenty guests, then a talking machine
eras.text: Back on Thrill Jockey, Mouse on Mars first made an ensemble record with 20-plus guests at footwork tempo, then an album about artificial intelligence built on software that talks. Their own MoMinstruments software and object-based spatial mixing were part of the kit.

years.src: Thrill Jockey: Dimensional People · Wikipedia: Mouse on Mars
years.h: Justin Vernon, the Dessners and Swamp Dogg join Dimensional People
years.p: Mouse on Mars' return to Thrill Jockey also brings in [[Zach Condon|f358bc90-dcb9-4ecb-bac6-55d52ba755c9]], [[Lisa Hannigan|8d0d65cf-3d01-4110-bf36-7e1aa27b68f2]], [[Sam Amidon|2e088ea8-b8f7-4df4-ac83-7024a50aabf1]] and about 20 more guests.
years.xp:
Most of it runs at 145 beats per minute, a tempo the duo took from Chicago footwork, inside one harmonic spectrum. Thrill Jockey describes it as a "dynamic 50-piece orchestra" laid out like a puzzle, with Ensemble Musikfabrik among the players and [[Aaron Dessner|1890e726-4817-42f4-92e7-ca78bef6692a]] and [[Bryce Dessner|20336142-85de-4e11-a1fd-a6c815b4e583]] of the National on the guest list.

It premiered as a spatial composition using object-based mixing, and was built to work as an installation and a performance as well as an album. The Dimensional People Ensemble played it live at the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg.

years.cap: Andi Toma, Dodo NKishi and Jan St. Werner, 2021
q: AI is capable of developing qualities we attach to humans
years.h: AAI teaches software to talk, then plays it like a synth
years.p: The voice models come from writer Louis Chude-Sokei and DJ Rayne. Dodo NKishi plays percussion and Casey Reas made the art.
years.xp:
The duo worked with the AI collective Birds on Mars and with former SoundCloud programmers Rany Keddo and Derek Tingle. DJ Rayne is Yağmur Uçkunkaya. The software's voice could be pushed faster or slower, happier or sadder, and the duo played it as an instrument.

St. Werner's argument: machines can "open up new concepts of life, and expand our definitions of being human." He wanted to get past the old fear of machines as competitors that do things faster or better.

years.h: Spatial, No Problem pairs Mouse on Mars with Lee "Scratch" Perry
years.p: Wikipedia lists the Domino album as a 2026 release. Perry, the dub pioneer, died in 2021.
